svg.title: The empirical rule on a normal curve
svg.desc: A normal curve with three nested shaded bands centred on the mean. The darkest band runs from one standard deviation below the mean to one above and holds about 68 per cent of the area. The next band extends to two standard deviations either side and holds about 95 per cent in total, not 95 per cent on top of the 68. The widest extends to three standard deviations and holds about 99.7 per cent. Each figure is the whole area from the left edge of that band to its right edge, so the bands contain one another rather than sitting side by side. About 0.3 per cent of the area lies beyond three standard deviations altogether. Illustrative data.
svg.text: How much of a normal distribution lies within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations
Each percentage is the WHOLE area inside that band, not an extra slice.
